title: Agency, Identity, Rights & Readiness

myths.myth: Your future is already decided for you.
myths.truth: You have real choices about your path.
myths.explanation: Agency is yours to build.

myths.myth: Big decisions should be made to please others.
myths.truth: Your informed choices matter most.
myths.explanation: It's your life and your body.

myths.myth: Asking about reproductive health is inappropriate at your age.
myths.truth: Knowing your body and rights is responsible.
myths.explanation: Information is protection.

myths.myth: There's a 'right' timeline for marriage, kids and career.
myths.truth: There's no single timeline.
myths.explanation: People thrive on very different paths.

myths.myth: Only certain people need to know their status.
myths.truth: Testing is for everyone who is sexually active.
myths.explanation: Knowing protects you and your partners.

myths.myth: HIV is a death sentence.
myths.truth: With treatment, people live long, healthy lives.
myths.explanation: Medicine has completely changed the picture.

myths.myth: You can get HIV from sharing food or hugging.
myths.truth: HIV doesn't spread through everyday contact.
myths.explanation: Facts end stigma.

myths.myth: Getting tested means you're 'dirty'.
myths.truth: Testing is responsible self-care.
myths.explanation: Stigma, not testing, is the real problem.

myths.myth: One person should lead and the other follow.
myths.truth: Healthy intimacy is mutual and respectful.
myths.explanation: Both people's comfort matters.

myths.myth: Talking about boundaries ruins the moment.
myths.truth: Communication makes things safer and better.
myths.explanation: Respect is attractive, not awkward.

myths.myth: If you don't resist, it counts as consent.
myths.truth: Only a clear, free yes is consent.
myths.explanation: Silence or fear isn't agreement.

myths.myth: Real partners just 'know' what you want.
myths.truth: People aren't mind-readers, so you communicate.
myths.explanation: Asking is a form of care.

myths.myth: There are only two genders and one 'normal' orientation.
myths.truth: Gender and orientation exist on a spectrum.
myths.explanation: Human diversity is real and natural.

myths.myth: Being LGBTQ+ is a phase or a choice.
myths.truth: Identity isn't a choice or a trend.
myths.explanation: People deserve respect as they are.

myths.myth: You can tell someone's identity by how they look.
myths.truth: You can't assume; people tell you who they are.
myths.explanation: Respect means listening.

myths.myth: Talking about this 'turns' kids a certain way.
myths.truth: Learning about diversity doesn't change anyone's identity.
myths.explanation: It just builds respect and safety.

myths.myth: Leadership comes more naturally to men.
myths.truth: Leadership is a skill anyone can build.
myths.explanation: History is full of leaders of every gender.

myths.myth: Ambitious women are 'too much'.
myths.truth: Ambition is a strength in anyone.
myths.explanation: The double standard is the problem, not the ambition.

myths.myth: There's no room at the top for everyone.
myths.truth: Inclusive leadership makes teams stronger.
myths.explanation: Diversity improves decisions.

myths.myth: You're too young to change anything.
myths.truth: Young people have driven huge change.
myths.explanation: Voice and action have no age limit.

myths.myth: Being an ally means speaking for others.
myths.truth: It means listening and amplifying.
myths.explanation: Support, but don't take over.

myths.myth: Change requires grand gestures.
myths.truth: Small, consistent actions add up.
myths.explanation: Movements are built from everyday choices.

myths.myth: Laws protecting equality don't really exist here.
myths.truth: India has laws on harassment, domestic violence, equality and child protection.
myths.explanation: Knowing your rights is power.

myths.myth: Reporting never helps.
myths.truth: There are real channels: helplines, committees, police, courts.
myths.explanation: Help exists; access matters.

myths.myth: Rights are only for adults.
myths.truth: Children and teens have rights too.
myths.explanation: The UNCRC and POCSO protect young people.

myths.myth: Getting help means shame.
myths.truth: Seeking justice is your right.
myths.explanation: The wrong belongs to the person who caused harm.

myths.myth: Adulthood means having it all figured out.
myths.truth: Everyone is still learning.
myths.explanation: Skills build over time.

myths.myth: Asking for help is for kids.
myths.truth: Knowing when to ask is a life skill.
myths.explanation: Independent doesn't mean alone.

myths.myth: Emotions get in the way of good decisions.
myths.truth: Naming emotions helps you decide well.
myths.explanation: Self-awareness is a tool, not a weakness.

myths.myth: You either have life skills or you don't.
myths.truth: Budgeting, planning and communication can all be learned.
myths.explanation: Practice is what makes you ready.

myths.myth: You can trust whatever's most viral.
myths.truth: Virality isn't credibility.
myths.explanation: Check the source, the date and the motive.

myths.myth: Deepfakes and AI images are easy to spot.
myths.truth: They're increasingly convincing.
myths.explanation: Verify before you believe or share.

myths.myth: Your data online is private by default.
myths.truth: Much of it is collected and sold.
myths.explanation: Privacy takes active choices.

myths.myth: Once you've learned this, you're done.
myths.truth: Media keeps changing; critical thinking is for life.
myths.explanation: Stay curious, keep questioning.

capstone.name: Ready for the World
capstone.landing: Sticker-book spread of every Ch.5 sticker earned; the erased myths of the whole Kids run shown as ghosts under fresh truths; a 'Ready for the World' badge; Lensy (with UN & RE) at the doorway where the corridor turns from light to dark: the hand-off into the Adult chapters.

canvasFeel: Kids/light, last light stretch, older-teen register: mature, candid, respectful of growing autonomy (agency, identity, rights, life-readiness). Gated/Sensitive nodes (g29, g30, g31) framed around consent, communication, health and rights, age-appropriate to India age-of-consent (18); optional guardian co-view flag. Capstone visibly previews the turn to the Adult/dark canvas. Tap struck myth -> UN erases -> RE writes -> sticker may drop.
